transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Daniel Kim, Priya Shah (Nova Systems)

Summary:
Quick intro, scope POC success criteria (latency, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy/regression), workload sizing, define benchmark plan, and timeline. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, batching/KV cache, quantization impact, and security/questions around VPC/SOC2. Ended with concrete next steps to share pricing and run a 1-week benchmark on Dedicated.

Topics:
- Success criteria and KPIs
- Workload sample distribution and sizing
- Per-token unit economics and batching/caching knobs
- Benchmark plan and timeline
- Security and deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok thanks everyone for jumping on, we'll keep this tightly scoped, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE, Samir our SE is here; Lina?
[00:08] Lena: thanks Maya, yeah I'm Lena, head of ml at Nova, we're evaluating infra for conversational assistants and doc QnA, main concerns are latency and cost, we have a 100k monthly active users estimate, but peak concurrency is the tricky bit
[00:20] Samir: awesome, quick qual question, are you currently using any managed LLM provider in prod?
[00:25] Priya: right now it's mixed - some experiments with OpenAI for prototypes, some on-prem older models, want to move to a predictable cost model and better SLOs
[00:36] Maya: got it. high level POC goals, we typically validate three things: 1) performance (p50/p95 latency), 2) cost/unit economics per token and per request, 3) functional/regression metrics vs your current baseline. what are your target numbers?
[00:52] Lena: for chat we're aiming for p50 <200ms and p95 <600ms for short-turn interactive queries; budget-wise we'd like per-1M-token cost under $30 if possible, but that's flexible depending on accuracy and latency
[01:10] Daniel: just to add, our token mix is skewed: 60% short chats (~50 tokens), 30% medium (~300 tokens), 10% long (~1k tokens). Peak qps estimate is 80 rps sustained for 10 minutes bursts.
[01:24] Samir: that's great detail, helps sizing. rough back-of-envelop, on Redwood Dedicated using a fp16-optimized open model variant with quantization we typically see X tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length. we'll run exact numbers in the benchmark. batching and KV cache will materially reduce per-token cost for those medium/long flows.
[01:44] Priya: can you explain the KV cache effect again? I think that's where we get savings for longer conversations?
[01:49] Samir: yeah, so KV cache means when a user continues a conversation we avoid re-computing attention for the prefix; for streaming chat it reduces decode work and lowers latency. Practically that can drop effective tokens processed by 20-40% when you have repeated prefixes and multi-turn. also prefix caching and partial result caching are options. sometimes the transcription labels this wrong, we saw "KV cash" in other notes ha.
[02:10] Lena: ha, "KV cash" :) ok. on cost modeling, what inputs do you need from us?
[02:16] Maya: sample logs with token counts, distribution (you gave that), and an SLA target. We'll feed that into our cost model that considers model selection (e.g. open-llama vs larger gpt-like variant), quantization (8-bit/4-bit), batching parameters, and autoscaling policy. We'll output per-request and per-1M-token projections.
[02:33] Daniel: curious about the dedicated vs hosted tradeoff. We have security regs — prefer VPC and audit logs — but Dedicated seems more expensive.
[02:40] Maya: right. hosted is fastest to get up and cheap for low volume. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; for your bursty 80 rps we usually recommend Dedicated or reserved pools with burst capacity. Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option if they need network isolation and on-prem certs; that adds integration time. We'll include cost delta in the pricing sheet.
[02:58] Priya: do you support SSO/SAML and KMS? compliance is a big ask for procurement
[03:03] Samir: yes SOC2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations are available. we'll share the security pack (SOC2 report + network diagram + SSO guide) after this call.
[03:14] Maya: to make the benchmark realistic we propose a 1-week run on Redwood Dedicated using your sample workload. Scope: run 3 model variants (smaller quantized, mid-size, and a high-accuracy variant), measure p50/p95, throughput, and cost/1M tokens with batching and with caching toggled. Does that sound ok?
[03:33] Lena: yes. timeline wise when can we start?
[03:35] Samir: we can provision a Dedicated test pool within 7-10 business days once we have the representative logs and a signed short POC addendum. baseline run takes 3-5 days, we recommend a full week to cover traffic variations.
[03:48] Daniel: and what will you need from our infra team for VPC peering?
[03:51] Samir: we have two options: Managed VPC peering for dedicated or a private deployment. For peering we need CIDR ranges, peering contact, and a jump box IP if you want restricted egress. we'll send the network checklist.
[04:03] Priya: on cost numbers, you mentioned $30 per 1M tokens target — is that with batching and 8-bit quant?
[04:09] Maya: that target is plausible for mid-size models with aggressive quantization and batching. We usually provide two scenarios: conservative (higher perf configs, minimal quant) and optimized (quantized + caching + larger batch sizes). We'll show both in the pricing sheet so you can pick tradeoffs.
[04:24] Lena: what about latency impact of batching? we can't exceed p50 200ms target
[04:28] Samir: batching trades latency for throughput. for short-turn chats we bias towards smaller batch sizes and lower latency SLOs; for embedding or bulk jobs we use large batch sizes. We'll tune batch windows (e.g., 5-10ms) and dynamic batching to keep p50 under your target while improving throughput at p95 window. We'll also test the model variants with and without batching in the benchmark.
[04:49] Maya: question for you on success criteria: besides latency and cost, do you need a specific QA/regression pass rate? like no more than X% drop vs your current prod in key intents?
[05:00] Lena: yes, we'd like less than 3% regression on intent accuracy across our top 20 prompts. we'll provide eval prompts.
[05:07] Samir: perfect — include that in the benchmark harness so we can run automatic evals and flag regressions.
[05:12] Priya: any gotchas on token accounting? some providers count tokens differently which affects cost comparisons
[05:17] Maya: good call — we'll normalize across tokenizers (we'll use BPE counts aligned to a shared tokenizer) and show per-token costs normalized to your tokenization.
[05:25] Daniel: who will own the benchmark scripts?
[05:28] Samir: Redwood will provide the harness and scripts; we'll ask you to run them in a controlled environment or have us run them against a dedicated pool. we'll include scripts, and a shared spreadsheet for results.
[05:40] Priya: sample artifacts to be shared?
[05:42] Maya: pricing spreadsheet, POC template, security pack, benchmark harness link (we'll put in a google drive / confluence). we'll link them in follow-ups: https://redwood.example.com/poc-pack and the benchmark sheet (link shared in the notes).
[05:58] Lena: great. procurement question, if we like the results what's typical ramp to prod?
[06:03] Maya: after successful POC we recommend a 6-8 week integration for a production rollout with Dedicated or Private depending on your choice — includes SSO/KMS setup, observability hooks (Redwood Console), and rollout policy config. If you go hosted small pilot can be quicker.
[06:18] Daniel: pricing model: do you do committed reserved capacity discounts?
[06:21] Maya: yes Dedicated offers reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual commits) with discounts; the pricing sheet will show reserved vs on-demand.
[06:29] Priya: any competitors we should be aware of? we evaluated OpenAI and AWS before — curious how you compare on unit economics
[06:35] Samir: comparison depends on model choice; OpenAI's managed endpoints are convenient but cost per token varies and limited control over batching/quantization. Bedrock/Vertex give ops control but often more ops overhead. We'll include a rough competitive benchmark in the materials.
[06:48] Lena: ok let's recap next steps...
[06:51] Maya: recap: we'll send pricing sheet, POC checklist, and security pack by 2026-03-05. You (Lena) will share anonymized chat logs and eval prompts by 2026-03-10. Samir will provision Dedicated test pool and run 1-week benchmark week of 2026-03-16. Action items captured in the notes.
[07:07] Priya: sounds good. any final Qs?
[07:10] Daniel: no, thanks all.
[07:11] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the shared links. Bye

Notes about transcription: minor mis-hearings present ("KV cash", some speaker label flips) consistent with automated transcription.

End of call.
